# Chain nutrition rollout: production results

<!-- Generated by the task receipt renderer from completed rollout journals. -->

**39,847 existing menu rows updated in 42 completed batches.**
Including the earlier WaBa/Yoshinoya work, the latest full audit found **40,505 approved exact matches, all consistent**.
Remaining chain source coverage is still being evaluated.

## Latest additions

| Chain | Rows updated | Facts / aliases | IDs preserved | Unselected rows unchanged |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| JINYA Ramen Bar | 226 | 57 / 73 | 448 | 222 |
| Noah's Bagels | 48 | 7 / 8 | 461 | 413 |
| Jack in the Box | 1,062 | 35 / 62 | 6,179 | 5,117 |

All passed a canary covering every fact represented in April menus, authenticated full-menu reads, search/detail consistency, and zero-change reruns.
Their original unreviewed catalog records and non-official estimates remain preserved.

JINYA uses 57 facts from its original published nutrition table.
Twenty topping facts assume one standard separately ordered portion because the source does not publish weights.
Merchant calorie labels establish agreement for named orders, not independent nutrition measurement.
The ambiguous Large versus Regular Impossible bowl remains estimated.

Noah's uses seven fixed servings from its branded 2026 PDF, with all 28 macro cells visually checked.
The standard Double-Stack has one published portion, while other egg sandwiches retain unresolved one- or two-egg choices.
Conflicting cookie values, inconsistent cinnamon/pastrami macros, and uncertain bundled sides remain estimated.
Fruity Cereal Pop has a published reference and an April menu entry but appears in neither current UE capture.

Jack in the Box uses 35 standard servings from its official 2026 guide.
The batch changes 933 numeric tuples and adds reviewed attribution to 129 unchanged tuples.
Conflicting breakfast facts, ambiguous sizes and bundles remain estimated.

## Same catalog for existing menus and new imports

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[Official source and serving review] --> C[Approved facts and exact aliases]
  C --> A[Existing April menu update]
  C --> U[UE import for a new location]
  A --> P[Stored menu macros and estimates]
  U --> P
  P --> API[Search and restaurant detail]
```

These additions use the already released matcher and writers from [PR302](https://github.com/dgmolla/fitsy/pull/302), reviewed at `e805ee2c63ec4e0f19563c6b8ff9fc4a8a3c121d`.
These were data updates; no new API deployment or menu-identity migration was required.
Offline imports and backfills must use a checkout containing this release.
Older writers and the chain-unaware rerun command must not rewrite reviewed menus.
Matching makes no LLM call; unmatched UE items continue to estimation.
Catalog loading and write validation add database work.
Activating a chain switches its menu source from the legacy FatSecret-first route to UE, so partially covered chains can require more estimation than before.
Net throughput of a complete production UE run has not been benchmarked.

| Local new-import proof | Captured UE items | Official matches | Historical menu rows replayed | Official matches |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| JINYA Ramen Bar | 199 | 109 | 448 | 226 |
| Noah's Bagels | 160 | 12 | 461 | 48 |
| Jack in the Box | 331 | 54 | 6,179 | 1,062 |

The tests exercised actual parsing, matching, selective estimation, brand handoff, food filtering, persistence and served macros with retained UE responses.
Historical new-location responses and estimator fallbacks were synthetic.
No actual production hex was added, and these tests do not establish measured-food accuracy.

## Repeatable lessons and remaining work

- Validate the source brand, country, region and serving before matching a name.
- Keep parser extraction separate from source accuracy; two parsers can agree on a publisher's erroneous number.
- Check symbols and source typos before creating permanent keys, while retaining the literal source evidence.
- Use one explicit published default when supported; leave unresolved sizes, egg counts and bundle components estimated.
- Exact reviewed aliases remain conservative: a new recipe description or serving needs new evidence.
- Keep source onboarding offline, then reuse approved facts through both existing-menu and new-import paths.

Continue reviewing remaining official sources and defensible aliases.
The separate menu-source-ID migration and allulose handling remain local and unshipped; they are outside this data rollout.
The existing title-based ingestion can still collapse distinct raw UE products sharing a name, so these proofs do not establish complete raw-product preservation.
